examples.en: My brother-in-law drove me to the airport.
I sometimes go fishing with my brother-in-law.
My older sister got married, so I gained a brother-in-law.
My brother-in-law works hard at his company.

examples.ko: 주말에 매형 집에 가서 조카를 만났어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went to my brother-in-law's house and saw my nephew.

examples.ko: 이사할 때 매형에게 부탁했더니 바로 도와줬어요.
examples.en: I asked my brother-in-law and he helped right away.

explain: 남자가 누나의 남편을 부르는 말이에요. 여자가 언니의 남편을 부르면 '형부'예요. 직접 부를 때는 '매형'이나 '형님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is what a man calls his older sister's husband. A woman calls her older sister's husband 형부. To his face, people say 매형 or 형님.

en: to be unkind; to be unfriendly

examples.ko: 그 가게 직원은 너무 불친절해서 다시 가기 싫어요.
examples.en: The staff at that shop were so unfriendly that I do not want to go again.

examples.ko: 불친절한 택시 기사를 만나서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: I met an unfriendly taxi driver and felt bad.
The restaurant owner was unfriendly to the customers.
If the staff are unfriendly, customers will decrease.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 사진은 예쁜데 서비스가 불친절해요.
examples.en: The photos of this hotel are pretty, but the service is unfriendly.

examples.ko: 불친절하다는 이야기를 듣고 후기를 다시 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard it was unfriendly, so I read the reviews again.

explain: '친절하다'의 반대말이고, '불-'은 '불가능', '불행'처럼 반대를 만들어요. 가게 직원이나 서비스의 태도를 말할 때 어울려요. 성격이 정이 없어 보이는 사람은 '무뚝뚝하다'고 해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '친절하다', and '불-' makes opposites as in '불가능' and '불행'. It fits the attitude of shop staff or a service. A person who seems cold by nature is called '무뚝뚝하다'.

examples.ko: 새언니가 저한테 예쁜 가방을 선물해 줬어요.
examples.en: My brother's wife gave me a pretty bag as a present.
My sister-in-law is really good at cooking.

examples.ko: 새언니, 이번 주말에 우리 집에 오실 거예요?
examples.en: Sister-in-law, will you come to our house this weekend?
My brother and his wife got married last year.
I get along very well with my sister-in-law.
I bought baby clothes for my sister-in-law.

explain: 오빠의 아내를 여동생이 부르거나 가리키는 말이에요. 남동생이 형의 아내를 부를 때는 '형수님'이라고 해요. 호칭으로도 그대로 써서 '새언니'라고 부르면 돼요.
explain_en: A younger sister uses this for her older brother's wife. A younger brother calls his older brother's wife '형수님' instead. It also works directly as a form of address: you can just call her '새언니'.

examples.en: My grandmother adores her granddaughter.
The granddaughter came to visit her maternal grandparents' house during vacation.
I am my grandmother's only granddaughter through her daughter.
The whole family gathered for the granddaughter's first birthday party.
I gave my granddaughter a little allowance.
My granddaughter has already become an elementary school student.

explain: 딸이 낳은 딸을 말해요. 아들이 낳은 딸은 '손녀'나 '친손녀'라고 하고, 딸이 낳은 아들은 '외손자'예요. 일상에서는 그냥 '손녀'라고 할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It means a daughter's daughter. A son's daughter is '손녀' or '친손녀', and a daughter's son is '외손자'. In everyday talk people often just say '손녀'.

examples.ko: 장인어른은 사위가 창업한다고 하자 처음에는 말리셨어요.
examples.en: When his son-in-law said he would start a business, his father-in-law at first tried to stop him.
The father-in-law and son-in-law go fishing together.
At the holiday I gave my father-in-law some spending money.

examples.ko: 장인어른이 직접 담근 김치를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father-in-law sent me kimchi he made himself.

examples.ko: 처음 장인어른을 뵈러 가던 날 너무 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was so nervous the day I first went to meet my father-in-law.
The whole family gathered for my father-in-law's birthday.

explain: 아내의 아버지를 높여 부르는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아버님'이라고 해요. 남편의 아버지는 '시아버지'이고, 부를 때는 마찬가지로 '아버님'이에요.
explain_en: It is a respectful word for one's wife's father. When addressing him directly, people usually say '아버님'. A husband's father is '시아버지', also addressed as '아버님'.

examples.en: My great-grandfather is ninety this year.

examples.ko: 명절에는 온 가족이 증조할아버지 댁에 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays the whole family gathers at my great-grandfather's house.
My great-grandfather told us stories from the old days.

examples.ko: 저는 증조할아버지를 한 번도 만나 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never met my great-grandfather.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 증조할아버지가 젊었을 때 찍은 거예요.
examples.en: This photo was taken when my great-grandfather was young.
My great-grandfather and great-grandmother farmed in their hometown.

explain: 윗사람이라서 '이/가' 대신 '께서'를 쓰고, '먹다'는 '드시다'처럼 높여 말해요. 어머니의 할아버지는 보통 '외증조할아버지'라고 해요. 짝말은 '증조할머니'예요.
explain_en: Because he is an elder, use '께서' instead of '이/가' and honorific verbs like '드시다' for 'eat'. Your mother's grandfather is usually called '외증조할아버지'. The female counterpart is '증조할머니'.

en: to approve; to consent; to permit

examples.en: My parents allowed me to take the trip alone.

examples.ko: 선생님이 수업 중에 사진 찍는 것을 허락해요.
examples.en: The teacher allows taking photos during class.
Nobody has allowed it yet.

examples.ko: 사장님이 허락하면 내일 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the boss allows it, I can take tomorrow off.

examples.ko: 관리실에서 여기에 짐을 두는 것을 허락해 줬어요.
examples.en: The management office allowed us to leave our things here.
I'll wait until Dad gives permission.

explain: '허락'은 부모님·선생님 같은 사람이 해 주는 것이고, 관청이 내주는 건 '허가'예요. 해 주는 쪽은 '허락하다', 받는 쪽은 '허락을 받다'라고 해요. 친구 사이에서는 '허락' 대신 '해도 돼요?'라고 물어요.
explain_en: 허락 comes from a person such as a parent or teacher, while permission issued by an authority is '허가'. The giver says '허락하다' and the receiver says '허락을 받다'. Between friends people usually just ask '해도 돼요?' (may I?).

p.n: The other word is stiffer, like agreeing to a formal request.
